objective.statement: Identify chords and their inversions in a short passage, and write them.
successCriteria: I gather the notes of a chord from both staves.
I find the root and then the lowest note.
I name every chord with its Roman numeral and position.

explanation.text: In a passage the notes of one chord are spread over two staves: the lowest note is usually on the lower stave, the others on the upper stave. To identify a chord, gather all its notes, ignore which stave each is on, and ignore any doubled notes. Then find the root by stacking thirds, and look at the LOWEST note for the position.

music.textAlternative: Four chords of C major, one in each bar: I, IV, V in second inversion (D lowest), then I.

explanation.caption: I, IV, Vc and I in C major. The V chord has D, its 5th, in the bass.

explanation.text: A passage may show the chords with Roman numerals and letters, such as I, ii, Vb, I. You may be asked to identify the chords (and their positions) or to write a chord on the stave. You will not be penalised for poor spacing; what is tested is whether you understand the basic chords and the position.
Collect the notes, find the root (a stack of thirds), then look at the lowest note: root a, third b, fifth c.

music.textAlternative: A chord of G major in the bass clef: G, D, B from the bottom up.

steps: Notes: G, D, B. Stack in thirds: G B D.
The root is G: chord I.
The lowest note is G, the root: Ia.
demonstration.textAlternative: G major chord in root position.
